title: Early Islam in Makkah
era: The First Three Years of Islam
teaser: Seven people stood up first. Seven against the world. Then came the persecution.

layers.title: The First Believers
layers.subtitle: Those who said yes when everyone said no
layers.content:
The very first to believe were those closest to the Prophet ﷺ. Khadijah bint Khuwailid was the first — his wife and his confidant. Then Ali ibn Abi Talib, a boy in the Prophet's household. Then Zayd bin Harithah, his freed slave. Then Abu Bakr as-Siddiq.

Abu Bakr then went to work. He went to Uthman bin Affan, Az-Zubayr bin Al-Awwam, Abd ar-Rahman bin Awf, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas and Talhah bin Ubaydullah. They all embraced Islam.

Among the early converts, there was a group who had unfortunately no strong clan at their back to support them. These innocent souls were ridiculed and taunted in season and out of season. The elite Quraish nobles used to ask with jest and disrespect: 'Has Allah favored these from amongst us?'
layers.quran_ref: Quran 6:53 — 'Does not Allah know best those who are grateful?'
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: The Call Goes Public
layers.subtitle: Mount Safa — the day everything changed
layers.content:
For three years, the call to Islam was conducted in secret. Then the command came: 'And warn your closest kindspeople.' (26:214)

The Prophet ﷺ climbed Mount Safa and called out: 'O Bani Fihr! O Bani Adi!' — until they gathered. He said: 'If I told you there was a horseman in the valley about to raid you, would you believe me?' They said: 'Yes, for we have never known you to lie.' He said: 'Then I warn you of a severe punishment before me.'

Abu Lahab said: 'Perish you all this day! Is this why you gathered us?' And Allah revealed: 'Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he!' (111:1)

From that day, the call was public. And the resistance became organised.
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: The Opposition
layers.subtitle: How Quraysh fought the message
layers.content:
The Quraysh used three tactics to resist Islam:

First — mockery and ridicule. They would wink to each other when believers passed, saying: 'Verily these have gone astray.' They called the Prophet ﷺ a madman, a poet, a soothsayer — anything to make the public dismiss him without engaging the message.

Second — distortion. They spread that the Quran was 'tales of the ancients' he had written down. That 'it is only a human being who teaches him.' They purchased female singers to entertain people away from the message.

Third — social and economic pressure. They boycotted Muslim businesses. They pressured Muslim employees. Anyone of high birth who converted was threatened with ruin. Anyone of low birth who converted was beaten.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 83:29-33 — 'Those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed'
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: The Persecution
layers.subtitle: What they did to the weak
layers.content:
When mockery and social pressure failed, the Quraysh turned to physical torture.

Bilal ibn Rabah was taken by his master Umayya bin Khalaf to the scorching valley. A giant stone was placed upon his chest. He said: 'One. One.'

Ammar bin Yasir and his parents — Yasir and Sumayyah — were stretched on burning sand and beaten. The Prophet ﷺ passed by and could only say: 'O family of Yasir, be patient — your place is in Paradise.' Yasir died under torture. Sumayyah was bayoneted by Abu Jahl himself — the first martyr in Islam.

Khabbab bin Al-Aratt was seized by his hair, twisted by the neck, thrown into fire. His tormentors dragged him through the embers until his back was burnt.

The Prophet ﷺ himself was protected by the nobility of Abu Talib's clan. What he could not stop, he bore witness to.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 16:106 — 'Whoever disbelieved after belief — except him who is forced thereto and whose heart is at rest with faith'
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'O family of Yasir, be patient — your place is in Paradise' — Ibn Hisham 1/320
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: What the early persecution built
layers.content:
The first Muslims were not powerful people using power to spread a message. They were weak people enduring power to preserve one.

Bilal's 'One. One.' under torture became the first adhan on top of the Ka'bah at the Conquest of Makkah — his voice calling the world to the One he refused to deny.

Sumayyah's death was not a tragedy that Islam overcame — it was the price that Islam was built on. The scholars say: the blood of the martyrs is the seed of the ummah.

Every person who was tortured for Islam in Makkah lived to see the Conquest — or died in a state that guaranteed them a higher station than conquest. The 'weak' of the early period became the foundation of everything that came after.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 2:155-157 — 'We will surely test you with fear and hunger and loss — but give good tidings to the patient'
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

quiz.prompt: Who was the first martyr in Islam?

options.text: Bilal ibn Rabah
Yasir ibn Amir
Sumayyah bint Khabbat
Ammar ibn Yasir

quiz.citation: Ibn Hisham 1/320 — Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: Sumayyah was bayoneted by Abu Jahl himself. She is honoured as the first shaheed in Islam.

quiz.prompt: What did the Prophet ﷺ say to the family of Yasir while they were being tortured?

options.text: I will negotiate for your release
Be patient — your place is in Paradise
Allah will punish those who do this
Conceal your faith to protect yourself

quiz.scholar_reflection: He could not stop the torture. He offered what he could — the certainty of where they were going.

quiz.prompt: Which tactic did An-Nadr bin Harith use to fight the message of Islam?

options.text: Physical torture of Muslims
Economic boycott
Telling Persian tales to distract audiences after the Prophet spoke
Approaching the Roman authorities

quiz.citation: Ibn Hisham 1/299-300 — Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: He learned Persian stories and followed the Prophet ﷺ from gathering to gathering, telling them afterward. Entertainment as inoculation against truth.

quiz.prompt: What did the Prophet ﷺ say from Mount Safa before announcing prophethood publicly?

options.text: I am the Messenger of Allah to all of you
If I told you there was a raider in the valley, would you believe me?
Abandon your idols and worship Allah alone
The punishment of Allah is near

quiz.scholar_reflection: He established his credibility first. They confirmed: we have never known you to lie. Then he gave the warning. He did not ask them to believe something new — he asked them to trust someone they already knew.

quiz.prompt: Who was Bilal's master who tortured him in the valley?

options.text: Abu Jahl
Abu Lahab
Umayya bin Khalaf
Uqba bin Abi Muayt

quiz.citation: Talqih Fuhum Ahlil-Athar p.61 — Ibn Hisham 1/317-318
quiz.scholar_reflection: Umayya bin Khalaf. He was later killed at Badr — by Bilal's request. The man who placed a stone on Bilal's chest was cut down on the day Islam's power became visible.

quiz.prompt: The first Muslims were mostly powerless people. Allah chose the weak as the vessel for the greatest message in history. What does this tell you about how Allah uses people?

options.text: Worldly power is irrelevant to Allah's plan
The weak were chosen because their sincerity could not be questioned
Allah protects what He uses — they endured because He sustained them
All of these cannot be separated

quiz.citation: Quran 8:26 — 'Remember when you were few and oppressed in the land'
quiz.scholar_reflection: The first Muslims had no armies, no wealth, no political protection. And they changed the world. Not because of what they had — because of what they refused to give up.

quiz.prompt: Ammar ibn Yasir uttered words of disbelief under torture while his heart remained firm in faith. Allah then revealed: 'except him who is forced thereto and whose heart is at rest with faith.' What does this reveal about how Allah judges?

options.text: Allah judges the heart, not only the tongue
Necessity has its own rulings in Islam
The body and the heart can be in different places
All of these — they are different aspects of the same truth

quiz.scholar_reflection: The verse was revealed for Ammar specifically — but it stands for every Muslim who has ever been forced into something while their heart remained elsewhere.

quiz.prompt: The Prophet ﷺ passed by the family of Yasir being tortured and could only promise Paradise. He did not intervene. What do you make of the limits of even the Prophet's ability to protect those he loved?

options.text: Some tests are given precisely because no human can remove them
The promise of Paradise in that moment was greater than any rescue
His own protection depended on his uncle — he was not free from vulnerability either
Powerlessness was part of the test for the Prophet ﷺ too

quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet ﷺ wept for those he could not protect. He did not pretend power he did not have. He gave what he had — certainty about what came next.

quiz.prompt: Bilal's 'One. One.' under torture and his adhan on top of the Ka'bah at the Conquest are the same voice, two decades apart. What does this continuity tell you about perseverance?

options.text: The same quality that made him endure made him worthy of the honour
His 'One' in the valley was already the adhan — he just hadn't climbed the Ka'bah yet
What you hold to in the darkest moment becomes your identity forever
Allah remembered what Bilal said in the desert and answered it at the Conquest

quiz.citation: Account of Bilal — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He said One under a stone. He said One from the top of the Ka'bah. The word never changed. Only his elevation did.

quiz.prompt: The Quraysh used entertainment, mockery, economic pressure, and physical torture — in that order — to resist Islam. What does this escalation tell you about how truth is opposed?

options.text: When a message cannot be defeated intellectually, physical force is the last resort
The escalation of resistance is proportional to the threat felt
Mockery is the first weapon because it requires no engagement with the argument
All of these — the sequence itself is a form of evidence

quiz.scholar_reflection: They never debated the message head-on. They mocked it, distorted it, economically pressured it, and finally tortured those who held it. The escalation tells you: the message was working.
